analysis:
Reconciled all three batch analyses against the available source replay; 23 source units were omitted, so their conclusions are not independently verified. No supported security regression was identified in the visible changes. These changes concern review infrastructure, not provider encryption, attestation, serving authorization, inference, cache isolation or payment-ledger behavior; no direct change to A-001/A-003, T-008, T-041 or T-053 is demonstrated.
.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml:64-73 removes paid dispatch and retains explicit fork opt-in for native AWS review. Lines 128-137 select a 3000-second deadline and workload-based native admission. .github/scripts/threat-model-review.py:16-23 bounds that deadline to 60–3000 seconds; lines 31-43 arm/cancel the alarm and report setup failure without claiming completion. bedrock.py:46-57 bounds native capacity to 500 calls and 16384 output tokens; lines 68-88 cumulatively plan stages, reserve one repair slot and make ceiling exhaustion sticky. These are intentional increases in paid resource exposure, not evidence of a budget bypass. Its new metrics are policy labels and integers, consistent with diagnostics.py:82-83 exporting those fields without new prompt or credential data.
Material integration questions remain: verify budget_scan.py's omitted scheduling paths admit every source/depth/integration call and enforce the single shared repair allowance; reconcile cache hits, native fallback and durable per-PR/run admission with the larger allowance. Verify budget_runner and threat-review-gate reject incomplete/stale results and treat finished as terminal execution, not successful clearance. The workflow removes dispatch but does not itself disable GitHub reruns; changelog.d/threat-review-automatic-completion.md:11 therefore depends on an admission control not visible here. These missing implementations and incomplete replay require further review, not vulnerability findings.
